note: Boat-ramp access on the point where Pointers Creek meets the Gasconade River, at the end of Route RA: one gravel lot with a privy and the ramp, and a designated primitive camping spot at the lot's edge. There are no pads; a rig camps on the ramp lot, which looks straight onto the river past the ramp. Route RA is impassable when Pointers Creek is at flood stage. --Claude
summary: Confirmed as far as MDC goes: 'Individual Campsites', one Primitive Camping Area symbol on the map beside the parking lot and one GIS point at the lot's edge. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. It is a 9-acre ramp access whose only hardstand is the ramp lot: lot-rule call for the owner. Stored riverfront does not meet the open-apron test (ramp and lot between): lead down to riverview. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - stays on the letter of the rule, owner's call): the area page lists 'Camping: Individual Campsites' and describes the area only as 'This area offers access to the Osage River with a boat ramp' (8.7 acres; no brochure). The map (06/08) draws one Primitive Camping Area symbol on the south side of the single Parking Lot symbol, beside the Privy and Boat Ramp symbols. GIS layer 27 has one 'Primitive Camping Area' point (OBJECTID 405) at 38.42511,-91.74283. On the 0.22 m/px leaf-off frame that point is in bottomland timber about 20 m north of the lot's edge, behind the privy, with no clearing, pad or track visible at it; the lot is one open gravel area about 40 x 30 m with the privy on its north side, a vehicle parked on it and the concrete ramp running off its east side into the river. So MDC does mark a designated camping point at the lot (GIS point at its edge and a map symbol beside it, as Lick Creek), which keeps it under the 2026-11-09 rule; but nothing sets the camping apart from the ramp lot, and a rig can only park on the lot itself (as Payne Landing). No wording like 'camping in the parking lot' or 'not recommended as a camping destination' appears, because there is no brochure. A 23-ft rig fits the lot.

WATERFRONT LEAD - DOWN (stored riverfront; evidence supports riverview): the designated point is in timber about 40 m from the Gasconade bank, but a rig cannot reach it; a rig stands on the ramp lot. From the lot the river is 10-25 m east and in plain view, but what lies between is the boat ramp and its turning apron, which is day use, so the open-apron test fails the same way it did at Payne Landing. South of the lot a line of bank trees separates it from Pointers Creek (about 15 m wide on the frame). Riverview is what the frame supports. The stored waterfront_evidence was not re-read against a pad because there is none.

NAME OF THE RIVER: the area page's one-line description says 'access to the Osage River', but the area map labels the water GASCONADE RIVER and the access is in Osage County on the Gasconade; the page line is an MDC slip. The note says Gasconade.

ACCESS: 'From Linn, take Route CC southeast 8 miles, then Route RA east to the access. (Route RA is impassable when Pointers Creek is at flood stage).' The map shows Route RA as Paved Road to the lot. No ford, 4WD wording or posted limit. Kept the flood caveat in the note.

PIN: stored 38.42511,-91.74283 is the GIS point, under canopy about 20 m north of the lot. Move onto the lot: 38.42486,-91.74260 (about 35 m; the centre of the gravel lot on the leaf-off frame; GIS lot 284 is at 38.42478,-91.74256).
PHONE: stored 573-815-7900 matches the area page ('For more information call (573) 815-7900').
